name: What is the best order for a living-space renovation?

mainEntity.name: Should flooring, painting, electrical, and built-ins happen in a specific sequence during an interior renovation?
mainEntity.text: Should flooring, painting, electrical, and built-ins happen in a specific sequence during an interior renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: A renovation should follow a logical sequence so trades do not undo each other’s work. In general, demo and structural changes happen first, followed by rough electrical, plumbing, or HVAC work if needed. After inspections, the project moves to insulation, drywall, finish carpentry, paint, flooring, and fixture installation. The exact order can change depending on materials and design details, but the principle is the same: complete messy work before delicate finishes. Homeowners should ask the contractor how they plan to sequence the job and whether any items need to be selected early to avoid delays. Proper sequencing protects the budget, reduces damage, and keeps the project moving efficiently.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, the order matters. Demolition and structural work come first, then rough electrical or mechanical changes, then drywall and finishes, and finally paint, flooring, trim, and fixtures depending on the project. A clear sequence reduces rework and helps avoid damaging finished surfaces.
